answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks via coastal microwave line-of-sight attestation. Nodes measure atmospheric phase delays of radio signals transmitted across a tidal lagoon to an antenna on an offshore island. Attackers incur the verifiable hardware and physical leasing costs of operating discrete microwave transceivers at separated coordinates per identity. However, shifting humidity and evaporative ducting introduce phase wander, occasionally triggering false rejections.
